items.basis: The candidate attributes clogging to "scale particles and biological growth" but the 20 percent flow boost mechanism increases throat transport velocity, which prevents particle settling yet does nothing to suppress biological growth; biofilm adhesion is governed by surface chemistry and nutrient availability, not convective shear at these velocities, so the mechanism cannot deliver the claimed reduction for a dual-mode failure. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "progressive nozzle clogging from scale particles and biological growth in the recirculated water degrades spray uniformity"

The candidate claims "header pressure stays 13-15 bar" while simultaneously claiming "raising header flow 20 percent using existing pump headroom"; for fixed-orifice flat-fan nozzles, flow scales with the square root of pressure, requiring a 44 percent pressure increase to achieve 20 percent more flow (1.2 squared equals 1.44), meaning starting from the stated 14 bar baseline the new pressure must be 20.16 bar, which violates the declared 13-15 bar boundary. GROUNDED_IN: COMPUTATION 14 bar times 1.2 squared equals 20.16 bar versus SCOPE "header pressure stays 13-15 bar"
